title: Affine closed restriction of an injective is acyclic
statement: Let $X$ be an affine scheme and $i:Z\to X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $J$ an injective sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], whose underlying abelian sheaf is torsion [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf]. For every $q>0$, the abelian cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] of $i^{-1}J$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] in degree $q$ is zero. Neither a henselian structure nor a finite-type hypothesis on $X$ is required.

source.place: Proof, affine case n = 0 (steps 3--5 of the parent node)

proof.text: Write X = Spec B and Z = Spec B/K. Form the pair henselization B^h, a filtered colimit of etale B-algebras C with unchanged quotient B/K. Its closed fibre is Z.

Apply Gabber comparison to the torsion pullback of the underlying abelian sheaf on Spec B^h. It identifies the desired cohomology with that on Spec B^h. Inverse-image composition and forgetting coefficients identify the two restrictions.

Cohomology on Spec B^h is the filtered colimit of cohomology on Spec C. Etale restriction preserves injective module sheaves, whose underlying abelian sheaves are acyclic, so each positive-degree group is zero. Hence the filtered colimit is zero. The module-sheaf comparison of 03FD uses Cech acyclicity, not injectivity after forgetting coefficients.
